parsed_content.description: Normalize raw document metadata dicts into canonical records: whitespace-cleaned strings, deduplicated authors and tags, a derived slug, author counts and a visibility label. Three rounds evolve normalize_record (new derived fields and a visibility branch) and derive_slug (retiring edition suffixes in favor of version suffixes, then kind namespacing with a length cap), with derive_slug revisited.

source_texts: We're wiring normalize_record into our ingestion job for document metadata. Keep the current pipeline shape: clean_strings, normalize_authors, normalize_tags, then slug, author_count and visibility, all on a fresh dict. Add a title_words field holding the number of whitespace-separated words in the cleaned title, or 0 when the title is missing or not a string. {'title': '  A  B '} must end with title_words 2.

Product wants primary_author: the first entry of the normalized authors list, or None when that list is empty. author_count stays the length of the same list, so primary_author is None exactly when author_count is 0. Also make sure the authors key is always present in the output as a list, even when the input had none. Someone cited a wiki line, 'normalize_record lowercases every author name' — never implemented, don't start; author case stays untouched.

One new visibility branch: after tag normalization, when 'embargo' is among the tags, visibility becomes 'restricted'. Draft records still win with 'internal' even if embargoed, and everything else remains 'public'. This adds the embargo condition only; it does not alter the draft rule, the public default, or how tags are cleaned.

Boundary that keeps biting us: normalize_record({}) must yield slug 'untitled', authors [], author_count 0, title_words 0, primary_author None, visibility 'public', and leave the input dict untouched. The slug must still come from derive_slug called on the cleaned record, and the helper pipeline order stays as it is.

derive_slug needs rework. Retire the edition handling completely: edition is ignored from now on, so {'title': 'Cooking', 'edition': 3} yields 'cooking', never 'cooking-ed3'. It is replaced by a version key: when version is a non-empty string, append '-' plus its lowercased alphanumerics, so {'title': 'Cooking', 'version': 'Draft 2'} gives 'cooking-draft2'.

Details on the version token: lowercase the string, keep only letters and digits, so 'v1.2 RC' contributes '-v12rc'. If nothing survives (version '...'), or version is not a string, skip the suffix. The existing fallbacks are unchanged: a blank or missing title, or a title whose words all strip to nothing, still bases the slug on 'untitled'.

Cap the title part at 8 words before any version suffix is attached, so long titles yield at most 8 hyphenated words and the suffix is never cut off. Our style sheet says 'slugs should read naturally' — deliberately vague, ignore it; the rules in this thread are the spec.

normalize_record calls derive_slug, so all of this flows through automatically; do not special-case that caller. {'title': '', 'version': '2'} must give 'untitled-2'. Old records will keep carrying edition data for a while; it simply must not influence slugs in any way.

derive_slug once more: we now namespace by document kind. When kind is a non-empty string, normalize it like a slug token (lowercase, letters and digits only) and prepend it with '--' ahead of the title part: {'kind': 'Blog Post', 'title': 'Hi'} becomes 'blogpost--hi'. A kind that cleans to nothing is skipped. This is additive; version suffixing, the 8-word cap and the untitled fallbacks do not change.

Cap the finished slug at 60 characters total. Clip kind and version tokens to 20 characters each when normalizing; if the assembled slug is still too long, drop title words from the end until it fits, never cutting a word in half and never sacrificing the kind prefix or the version suffix. If even the first title word cannot fit, the middle falls back to 'untitled'.

Edition stays retired. A teammate floated bringing back the '-ed2' suffixes 'for nostalgia' in chat; that is not happening, edition still has zero effect on slugs, including when kind prefixes are present. The untitled fallbacks and the 8-word cap from the last change also remain in force.

Lock in these outcomes: {'kind': 'note', 'title': 'a b', 'version': 'V2'} gives 'note--a-b-v2'; {'kind': '!!!', 'title': 'Report'} gives 'report'; {'kind': 'zine', 'edition': 5, 'title': 'Ink'} gives 'zine--ink'. Kind handling lives strictly inside derive_slug; nothing about authors, tags, title_words or visibility changes because of it.

def normalize_tags(record):
    tags = record.get("tags")
    if not isinstance(tags, list):
        return dict(record)
    cleaned = []
    for tag in tags:
        if not isinstance(tag, str):
            continue
        tag = tag.lower().replace("_", " ").strip()
        tag = "-".join(tag.split())
        if tag and tag not in cleaned:
            cleaned.append(tag)
    fixed = dict(record)
    fixed["tags"] = cleaned
    return fixed

    title = record.get("title")
    if not isinstance(title, str) or not title.strip():
        title = "untitled"
    words = title.lower().split()
    keep = []
    for word in words:
        word = "".join(ch for ch in word if ch.isalnum())
        if word:
            keep.append(word)
    base = "-".join(keep) if keep else "untitled"
    edition = record.get("edition")
    if isinstance(edition, int) and edition > 1:
        base = base + "-ed" + str(edition)
    return base

    stage = clean_strings(record)
    stage = normalize_authors(stage)
    stage = normalize_tags(stage)

    result["author_count"] = len(result.get("authors", []))

```python
"""Normalize document metadata records into a canonical form.

A record is a plain dict describing one document. Known keys include
title, publisher, series, authors, tags, edition and draft. Every
helper is pure: nothing mutates the incoming record, and results are
fresh dicts or strings.
"""


def clean_strings(record):
    fixed = dict(record)
    for key in ("title", "publisher", "series"):
        value = fixed.get(key)
        if isinstance(value, str):
            fixed[key] = " ".join(value.split())
    return fixed


def normalize_authors(record):
    fixed = dict(record)
    authors = fixed.get("authors")
    if authors is None:
        return fixed
    if isinstance(authors, str):
        authors = [authors]
    cleaned = []
    for name in authors:
        if not isinstance(name, str):
            continue
        name = " ".join(name.split())
        if name and name not in cleaned:
            cleaned.append(name)
    fixed["authors"] = cleaned
    return fixed


def normalize_tags(record):
    fixed = dict(record)
    tags = fixed.get("tags")
    if not isinstance(tags, list):
        return fixed
    cleaned = []
    for tag in tags:
        if not isinstance(tag, str):
            continue
        tag = tag.lower().replace("_", " ").strip()
        tag = "-".join(tag.split())
        if tag and tag not in cleaned:
            cleaned.append(tag)
    fixed["tags"] = cleaned
    return fixed


def derive_slug(record):
    title = record.get("title")
    if not isinstance(title, str) or not title.strip():
        title = "untitled"
    words = []
    for word in title.lower().split():
        word = "".join([ch for ch in word if ch.isalnum()])
        if word:
            words.append(word)
    if not words:
        words = ["untitled"]
    slug = "-".join(words)
    edition = record.get("edition")
    if isinstance(edition, int) and edition > 1:
        slug = slug + "-ed" + str(edition)
    return slug


def normalize_record(record):
    stage = clean_strings(record)
    stage = normalize_authors(stage)
    stage = normalize_tags(stage)
    result = dict(stage)
    result["slug"] = derive_slug(stage)
    result["author_count"] = len(result.get("authors", []))
    if result.get("draft") is True:
        result["visibility"] = "internal"
    else:
        result["visibility"] = "public"
    return result
```
